focus: Angle 5: skills, slash commands and subagents
noveltyJustification: Nine findings are fully new (skill metadata, dual invocation, discovery order, registry skills, task tool, subagent caps, repository skill/command/agent mapping); one is partially new because it corrects the prior Code Mode verdict from none to equivalent.
keyQuestions: How does Vibe run one task non-interactively: which prompt source, flags, output formats and exit codes does the headless contract expose?
Which providers, models and authentication paths can a Vibe dispatch use, and which usage counter does a turn draw on?
What does Vibe read from the working directory and ~/.vibe/, and what would a generated repo-root .vibe/ mirror contain?
For each cli-opencode surface this repository uses, does Vibe have an equivalent, a partial equivalent or none, and what would porting take?
What would a cli-mistral-vibe deep-loop executor kind need, and is ACP a better dispatch surface than print mode?
ruledOut: Treating the absence of .vibe/commands as proof of no slash commands: user-invocable skills are the slash surface
Reading the task tool as an unrestricted subagent dispatch: the default allowlist contains only explore

label: Vibe skills are YAML frontmatter plus a markdown body with name (lowercase hyphen, max 64), description (max 1024), optional license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools, user-invocable and disable-model-invocation.

Skills are model-invoked through the skill tool and user-invoked as /skill-name; user-invocable:false hides a skill from the slash menu and disable-model-invocation:true makes it user-only, so user-invocable skills are Vibe's slash commands.

Skill discovery order is skill_paths (global), then project .vibe/skills and .agents/skills, then user dirs, deduped by resolved path; the first claimant of a name wins and losers are reported shadowed.
Registry skills are opt-in: experimental_enable_registry_skills pulls versioned shared skills from Mistral with a latest alias and materialises them beside local skills.
Subagents are the task(task, agent=explore) tool returning response, turns_used and completed, with a permission allowlist defaulting to explore and a denylist.
The subagent roster is agent profiles with agent_type subagent, bounded by enable_subagents (true), max_subagents (32) and max_concurrent_subagents (32).
Repository skills map with near-zero effort by pointing skill_paths at .skilled/skills, since each is a SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter and extra keys are tolerated as metadata.
Repository commands do not map one-to-one: OpenCode commands take $ARGUMENTS, while a Vibe user-invocable skill body has no documented argument placeholder.

Repository agents map through a renderer: body to instructions, frontmatter to display_name/description/safety, subagent leaves get agent_type subagent plus a task allowlist entry, and main is a reserved name.

Correction: Vibe has a Code Mode equivalent, the run_typescript runtime builtin whose program-made calls carry parent_call_id and reach tools and subagents as tools.*, superseding iteration 4's none verdict.
